title: Check if Strings Can be Made Equal With Operations II
summary: Given two strings s1 and s2, both of length n and consisting of lowercase English letters, determine if it is possible to make s1 equal to s2 by performing the following operation any number of times: - Choose any two indices i and j such that i < j and the difference j - i is even, then swap the characters at these indices in the string.
statement: Given two strings s1 and s2, both of length n and consisting of lowercase English letters, determine if it is possible to make s1 equal to s2 by performing the following operation any number of times: - Choose any two indices i and j such that i < j and the difference j - i is even, then swap the characters at these indices in the string. Return true if the strings can be made equal, and false otherwise.
constraints: s1 and s2 have equal length and lowercase letters.
A swap may exchange positions whose index difference is even.
Return whether any sequence of allowed swaps transforms s1 into s2.
hints: An even index difference means both indices have the same parity.
Characters may permute freely within even positions and within odd positions, but cannot cross groups.
Compare the two multisets for each parity.
Equal multisets are necessary and sufficient because arbitrary permutations are generated by swaps within each group.
editorial: Equal multisets are necessary and sufficient because arbitrary permutations are generated by swaps within each group.

tests.explanation: Even positions and odd positions have matching character multisets, so transformation is possible.
The parity-position character multisets differ, so no allowed swaps can succeed.
